reading.body:
Steve Stombres is named on 32 Lobbying Disclosure Act filings about AI, filed through one lobbying firm, with ID.ME, LinkedIn, Maplebear, and Microsoft as the most frequent clients.

The record is concentrated. A single firm carries all 32 filings, and four clients account for 30 of the client mentions across them. The AI bills themselves are barely represented here: one bill, S 2296, appears, and only as a single named item. What the data establishes is a roster of who is being represented on AI, not what was said or sought.

The disclosed prior government positions are all congressional staff roles, chiefly Chief of Staff in the Majority Leader's and Whip's offices and for Eric Cantor, spanning 2001 to 2014. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires these to be listed for twenty years, so their presence is a disclosure requirement rather than a finding. The data does not show whether these relationships were used, or on which issues.

For AI specifically, the client list is the useful part. Identity verification, professional networking, grocery delivery, and cloud and software infrastructure are all represented, which places AI lobbying here in the application and platform layer rather than in data centers, power, or chip supply. Nothing in this record speaks to compute, buildings, or the grid. It also does not give dollar amounts, specific lobbying asks, or outcomes, and it covers only filings this site has classified as AI-related.

summary: Steve Stombres is named as a lobbyist on 32 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 61629. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
